next_question.rationale: Two rate-bearing cuts remain untried (hour_of_day, item_count). I recommend cutting by item_count next because it can reveal whether baskets of certain sizes systematically convert worse — which would interact with the stock_status and consultation_required gaps we already see and point to an operational fix (e.g., better handling of single-item RX orders or multi-item fulfillment). Evidence: top gap is from created->confirmed with lost=417569 (share_of_prev=0.6452) and funnel shows created=647191 -> confirmed=229622 (conversion_from_previous=0.3548). Consultation_required already shows a meaningful gap (rx_gated: entered=255293, converted=76641, rate=0.3002 vs non_rx: entered=391898, converted=152981, rate=0.3904). stock_status shows extremely low conversion for unfulfilled/partially-fulfilled baskets (has_unfulfilled_item: entered=19728, converted=1831, rate=0.0928; has_partially_fulfilled_item: entered=2191, converted=16, rate=0.0073), suggesting fulfillment issues tied to items in the basket. Cutting by item_count should help determine if low-conversion segments are concentrated in particular basket sizes (e.g., single-item RX vs multi-item orders), which is more actionable than hour_of_day for addressing fulfillment/consultation interactions.
